easy.def: To do what you are told.
examples: My dog will obey when I say "sit."
We obey the school rules.
The horse obeys the rider.

more.def: To do what a person, rule, or law tells you to do.
examples: Drivers must obey the traffic signs.
Soldiers must obey their orders.
The well-trained dog obeyed every command.

easy.def: A thing you can see and touch.
examples: A ball is a round object.
What is that object in the sky?
Put each object in the box.

more.def: A thing that you can see and touch, but that is not alive.
examples: There was a shiny object at the bottom of the pond.
Sharp objects should be kept away from babies.
A telescope helps you see objects in space.
We observe the ants as they work.
We observe the moon at night.
The cat observes the bird.

more.def: To watch someone or something closely in order to learn about it.
examples: The class observed how the caterpillar changed over two weeks.
Doctors observed the patient overnight.
If you observe the sky tonight, you may see a comet.

easy.def: A very big sea of salt water.
examples: Whales live in the ocean.
We swim in the ocean.
The ocean is very deep.

more.def: One of the huge bodies of salt water that cover most of the Earth.
examples: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
Sea turtles travel across the ocean to lay eggs.
From the plane, the ocean looked endless.

easy.def: Something that is as different as it can be.
examples: Hot is the opposite of cold.
Up is the opposite of down.
Big is the opposite of small.

more.def: A person or thing that is completely different from another.
examples: The opposite of "ancient" is "modern."
He said he was tired, but he acted the opposite.
My sister is the opposite of me: she loves mornings.

easy.def: To go around and around something in space.
examples: The Earth orbits the sun.
The moon orbits the Earth.
A spaceship orbits the planet.

more.def: To travel in a curved path around a planet, moon, or star.
examples: The moon orbits the Earth about once every month.
Many satellites orbit the Earth and send signals for phones.
It takes one year for the Earth to orbit the sun.

easy.def: A place where fruit trees grow.
examples: We picked apples in the orchard.
Pears grow in the orchard.
Birds sing in the orchard.

more.def: A piece of land where fruit or nut trees are grown.
examples: The orchard was full of ripe peaches.
The family runs a cherry orchard.
We walked between rows of trees in the orchard.
It was an ordinary day at school.
I wore my ordinary shoes.
He is an ordinary boy who loves soccer.

more.def: Usual or normal; not different or special in any way.
examples: It looked like an ordinary rock, but there was a crystal inside.
On an ordinary morning, I wake up at seven.
The hero of the story is an ordinary girl who does something brave.
Let's organize the toys by color.
I organize my crayons.
We organized a bake sale.

more.def: To arrange things in a neat order, or to plan an event.
examples: We organized the books by author on the shelf.
The students organized a clean-up day at the park.
She organized her notes before the test.
We like to play outdoors.
The dog sleeps outdoors.
It is cold outdoors today.
On sunny days, our class eats lunch outdoors.
The concert was held outdoors in the park.
He loves working outdoors on the farm.

easy.def: A part of air that we need to breathe.
examples: We need oxygen to live.
Trees make oxygen.
Fish get oxygen from water.

more.def: A gas in the air that people, animals, and plants need to live.
examples: Fish use their gills to take oxygen from the water.
Divers carry tanks of oxygen.
Your blood carries oxygen to every part of your body.
